intro: Above Altınoluk, on Kaletaşı hill in Balıkesir province, lies Antandros, an ancient city of the Troad whose story runs from the 8th century BC to the 4th century AD. It is known for its mosaic villas and its tomb necropolis.
history: People have lived here since the 8th century BC. The city was famed for its timber, which was used to build Persian warships. Under Rome it was adorned with luxurious villas, and since excavations began in 2001 they have been coming back to light.
structure-1: You are now at the Mosaic Roman Villa, a Roman-period residence adorned with floor mosaics. Look down and imagine the household that once walked across these floors.
structure-3: This is the Rural Villa, a Roman villa set in the farmland outside the city. Picture the fields that once surrounded it.
structure-4: Here are the Workshops, where craft and production activities took place. Imagine the sounds of work filling these spaces.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Necropolis and the City Walls.
facts: Did you know? The 'Abduction of Europa' mosaic in the Roman villa at Antandros, found in 2005, counts among Turkey's most important mosaic discoveries. In Virgil's Aeneid, it was right here that Aeneas built the ships he fled Troy in, from the timber of Mount Ida. And the mosaics and wall paintings of an excavated Roman villa record a life of coastal luxury at the foot of the Kaz mountains.
outro: This brings our journey through Antandros to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
